abstract: Ab initio computation of molecular properties is one of the most promising applications of quantum computing. While this problem is widely believed to be intractable for classical computers, efficient quantum algorithms exist which have the potential to vastly accelerate research throughput in fields ranging from material science to drug discovery. Using a solid-state quantum register realized in a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) defect in diamond, we compute the bond dissociation curve of the minimal basis helium hydride cation, HeH+. Moreover, we report an energy uncertainty (given our model basis) of the order of $10^{-14}$ Hartree, which is ten orders of magnitude below desired chemical precision. As NV centers in diamond provide a robust and straightforward platform for quantum information processing, our work provides several important steps towards a fully scalable solid state implementation of a quantum chemistry simulator.

specification.problem: Compute the ground-state electronic energy E_0(R) of the helium hydride cation HeH+ in a minimal (assumed STO-3G) basis as a function of internuclear distance R (the bond dissociation curve), using a small quantum register (NV-center spins) and a phase-estimation-type eigenvalue algorithm whose energy uncertainty for the model Hamiltonian is of order 1e-14 Hartree.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction (assumption, no experiment_scope supplied): iterative phase estimation (IPEA) with one ancilla qubit and a 2-qubit system register encoding the four N=2, S_z=0 Slater determinants of minimal-basis HeH+, for a single internuclear distance R (e.g. R = 0.9 Angstrom) and a small number of phase bits (e.g. m = 4) as a tiny illustrative instance. The full dissociation curve is obtained by repeating the same procedure over a grid of R values. Out of scope: the specific NV-center physical encoding (electron/nuclear spin levels), pulse-level control, how the paper reaches ~47-bit (1e-14 Ha) precision, decoherence/error analysis, and any claims about classical intractability.

symbols.meaning: One- and two-electron integrals of HeH+ in the minimal orthonormal (molecular-orbital) basis, computed classically
Nuclear repulsion energy Z_{He} Z_{H}/R = 2/R (atomic units)
Fermionic creation/annihilation operators for spin-orbital p
symbols.domain: operators on 16-dim Fock space of 4 spin-orbitals

symbols.meaning: Slater determinants in the N=2, S_z=0 sector: |1\alpha1\beta\rangle, |1\alpha2\beta\rangle, |2\alpha1\beta\rangle, |2\alpha2\beta\rangle
4x4 Hermitian (real symmetric) matrix of the electronic Hamiltonian in the basis \{|\Phi_i\rangle\}
symbols.domain: real symmetric 4x4 matrix, entries in Hartree

symbols.meaning: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of H(R); E_0 is the ground-state energy
Evolution-time parameter chosen so that all relevant phases lie in [0,1)
Unitary e^{-iH(R)t} acting on the 2-qubit system register
Eigenphase of U associated with E_n, defined modulo 1
Number of phase bits extracted by IPEA
k-th measured phase bit (k=1 most significant)
Classical feedback rotation angle at IPEA iteration k

equations.label: Second-quantized molecular Hamiltonian
equations.latex: H_{el}(R) = \sum_{p,q=1}^{4} h_{pq}(R)\, a_p^\dagger a_q + \frac{1}{2}\sum_{p,q,r,s=1}^{4} h_{pqrs}(R)\, a_p^\dagger a_q^\dagger a_r a_s + E_{nuc}(R)
equations.description: Electronic-structure Hamiltonian in a fixed basis of 4 spin-orbitals (minimal basis for HeH+); the integrals h_{pq}, h_{pqrs} are classical inputs depending on R.
equations.justification: Standard starting point of ab initio quantum chemistry simulation; the abstract names the problem (minimal-basis HeH+) but not this formula.
assumptions: Born–Oppenheimer approximation
Minimal basis with one spatial orbital per atom (2 spatial / 4 spin-orbitals), e.g. STO-3G
Spin-orbitals orthonormalized (e.g. canonical Hartree–Fock orbitals)

equations.label: Symmetry-reduced 4x4 Hamiltonian and 2-qubit compact encoding
equations.latex: H(R)_{ij} = \langle \Phi_i | H_{el}(R) | \Phi_j \rangle,\quad i,j \in \{1,2,3,4\},\qquad |\Phi_i\rangle \mapsto |q_1 q_2\rangle \text{ with } i-1 = 2 q_1 + q_2
equations.description: Restriction of H_el to the N=2, S_z=0 subspace containing the ground state; the four determinants are mapped to the four 2-qubit computational basis states (register order q_1 q_2, q_1 most significant). H(R) = sum_{ij} H_ij |i-1><j-1| is the system Hamiltonian.
equations.justification: A smallest register that still contains the exact minimal-basis ground state; the abstract only says a 'solid-state quantum register' was used, so this encoding is a proposed construction, not sourced.
assumptions: Ground state lies in the N=2, S_z=0 sector (true for closed-shell singlet HeH+)
Matrix elements H_ij evaluated classically via Slater–Condon rules from h_pq, h_pqrs
Compact (configuration) encoding rather than Jordan–Wigner on 4 qubits

equations.label: Time-evolution unitary and eigenphase relation
equations.latex: U(R) = e^{-iH(R)t},\qquad U(R)|\psi_n\rangle = e^{-iE_n(R)t}|\psi_n\rangle = e^{2\pi i \phi_n}|\psi_n\rangle,\qquad \phi_n = \left(-\frac{E_n(R)\,t}{2\pi}\right) \bmod 1
equations.description: Eigenvalues of H are encoded as phases of U; the relation between phi_n and E_n is only defined modulo 1, so t (and an optional energy shift) must be chosen so the target phase is unambiguous.
equations.justification: Standard phase-estimation mapping between Hamiltonian eigenvalues and unitary eigenphases; the abstract does not state which eigenvalue algorithm was used.
assumptions: Since H(R) is a 4x4 matrix, U(R) and its powers U^{2^{k-1}} can be compiled exactly (classically) as 2-qubit unitaries, no Trotterization needed
t chosen so that |E_n t| < 2π for the eigenvalue of interest

equations.label: Iterative phase estimation (IPEA) iteration k
equations.description: For iteration k (processed from least to most significant bit): ancilla prepared in (|0>+|1>)/sqrt2, controlled-U^{2^{k-1}} applied to the system in eigenstate |psi_n>, ancilla phase gate diag(1, e^{i omega_k}) applied, Hadamard, then ancilla measured giving bit x_k. With exact eigenstate input the outcome is deterministic when 2^{k-1}phi_n plus the feedback is an exact binary fraction; otherwise the last bit is probabilistic.
equations.justification: Standard single-ancilla iterative phase estimation with classical feedback; it is the natural candidate for a few-qubit register reaching very high phase precision, but its use in the paper is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: System register prepared in (or with large overlap on) the target eigenstate |psi_0>
Bits x_{k+1..m} from previous iterations are used classically in omega_k

equations.label: Energy reconstruction and resolution
equations.description: The m measured bits form a binary fraction approximating phi_0 (truncation, not exact), converted back to an energy estimate; the resolution is set by 2^{-m}/t. The 1e-14 Hartree uncertainty quoted in the abstract corresponds, for t of order 1 a.u., to m on the order of 45–50 bits (inference, not a sourced number).
equations.abstract_quote: we report an energy uncertainty (given our model basis) of the order of $10^{-14}$ Hartree
equations.justification: The abstract reports an energy uncertainty; relating it to phase-bit resolution assumes a phase-estimation-type readout. The exact algorithmic source of the uncertainty is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Phase bits are extracted sequentially with negligible readout error
The uncertainty refers to algorithmic/statistical precision for the model Hamiltonian, not basis-set error

equations.label: Bond dissociation curve
equations.latex: E_0(R) = \min_n E_n(R) \text{ for } R \in \{R_1,\dots,R_N\},\qquad D_e = \lim_{R\to\infty} E_0(R) - \min_R E_0(R)
equations.description: The ground-state energy is estimated at each grid point R (requiring recompilation of U(R) and re-preparation of the input state), giving the dissociation curve; D_e is the resulting dissociation energy.
equations.abstract_quote: we compute the bond dissociation curve of the minimal basis helium hydride cation, HeH+
equations.justification: The abstract explicitly states the dissociation curve is computed; the equation formalizes 'curve' as E_0 sampled over R and the derived dissociation energy.
assumptions: A finite grid of R values is used
The large-R limit is approximated by the largest R on the grid

registers.name: ancilla
registers.role: Phase-estimation probe qubit: prepared in |+>, controls U^{2^{k-1}}, receives feedback phase, measured to yield bit x_k (written leftmost in |a> ⊗ |q_1 q_2>)

registers.name: system
registers.role: Encodes the four N=2, S_z=0 Slater determinants of minimal-basis HeH+ via i-1 = 2 q_1 + q_2; holds the (approximate) eigenstate on which U(R) acts

specification.initial_state: |0\rangle_a \otimes |\psi_{in}\rangle, with |\psi_{in}\rangle = |00\rangle = |1\alpha 1\beta\rangle (Hartree–Fock determinant, assumed to have large overlap with |\psi_0\rangle), or, since H(R) is 4x4, the exact |\psi_0(R)\rangle prepared by a classically compiled 2-qubit unitary (assumption).

steps.description: Classical pre-processing at fixed R: compute minimal-basis integrals h_pq(R), h_pqrs(R) and E_nuc(R); build the 4x4 matrix H(R) in the S_z=0 determinant basis; choose t; compile U(R)^{2^{k-1}} for k=1..m as exact 2-qubit unitaries.
Prepare the system register in the input state (Hartree–Fock |00> or the exact ground state) and the ancilla in |0>; set k = m and the bit record to empty.

IPEA iteration k: apply Hadamard to the ancilla, controlled-U(R)^{2^{k-1}} on the system, the feedback phase gate diag(1, e^{i omega_k}) on the ancilla, a second Hadamard, and measure the ancilla to obtain x_k; reset the ancilla; decrement k and repeat until k = 1.
Assemble the binary fraction from x_1..x_m and convert to the energy estimate E_0(R); repeat the whole procedure for each R on the grid to trace out the dissociation curve.

specification.measurement: Projective measurement of the single ancilla qubit in the computational basis at each IPEA iteration, yielding one phase bit x_k; m iterations per energy value. Repetition per bit (majority vote) is used if the input state is not an exact eigenstate.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compute omega_k from previously obtained bits (eq_4); form phi = sum_k x_k 2^{-k}; convert to E_0(R) = -2π phi / t (eq_5), undoing any energy shift used to place the phase in [0,1); tabulate E_0 versus R and extract the dissociation energy (eq_6).
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the chosen scope (IPEA, 1 ancilla + 2 system qubits, single R, small m) is the author's smallest-useful-construction choice, not derived from the abstract.
Minimal basis taken to be STO-3G (the abstract says only 'minimal basis').
Compact encoding of the S_z=0 two-electron sector on 2 qubits with ordering i-1 = 2 q_1 + q_2.
Because the Hamiltonian is a tiny matrix, U(R) and its powers are compiled exactly from the classically diagonalizable H(R); no Trotter error.
The reported ~1e-14 Hartree uncertainty is interpreted as the resolution of a many-bit phase estimate, which is an inference.
The NV-center specifics (which spin levels play ancilla/system roles) are not reconstructed.

The gate/pulse sequence implementing controlled-U^{2^{k-1}} and state preparation
